text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap The LED light is bright enough to help you get your key into a lock, but it'll only dimly light your path. The alarm sound is not very loud--not as loud as a car alarm or a whistle or a smoke alarm. It doesn't help that the speaker is on the back, where your hand naturally covers it to some degree. It makes a weird noise that didn't even grab the attention of a man sitting 70 feet away because it sounded like just another mechanical noise rather than an alarm. The stun gun made more noise! Personally, I'd hoped the light and the alarm noise would warn most potential attackers away, but I doubt they'll be much help. Since the light and the sound aren't as impressive as they advertised, I do wonder if the stun gun will be very effective, but I'm not going to test it out on anyone! They say it's most effective on certain parts of the body, so you have to be close and even aim somewhat, not just touch the current to some body part.

Anyway, you get a USB charging cord and have to charge the stun gun 12 hours before the first use and 4-5 hours each week. Though the green (full charge indicator) light turns on after only a couple hours, they stress the length of time spent on charging more than the indicator light. There is an on/off switch than must be turned on before the alarm sound or the stun gun button will work. The light button will work at all times. The buttons are easy to use, though the labeling on them is not easy to read (especially at night). The light stays on until pressed off, which means it can be turned on if something presses the button when in your purse. This could run the battery down so it's not effective when needed. Some way to check how much charge is left would have been useful. I've never seen or used a stun gun before, but this seemed more hype than useful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap

My wife and I have recently taken up the sport and wanted bags to not just carry our stuff, but store it off the court, and carry the various things we end up having with, based on that days activities. This JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag hits all the checks for us.

It has a great look. That dark blue and yellow-green are so nice together - they look good in pictures, but great in person. One wouldn’t think such a bright color would be appealing, but it is, and as my wife always points out, a lighter color for the interior of a bag makes it that much easier to see inside - including those dark corners. There are plenty of corners here. The inside of the main compartment has several pockets with zippers to keep things in place, offering places for things like wallet, keys, and other little items you end up carrying. Bring the extra set of clothes? There is plenty of room to keep things in place. This main compartment is huge and we can easily get in another set of clothes and even toiletry bag in there to make changing easy. There is one of those shoe slots - the in thing for all gym bags - which always take up space in the main bag, but keeps your shoes separate from your clothes - and there reminds plenty of room in the bag even when full. The shoe bag - accessed from the exterior - has a little venting hole for keeping smells in check. The zippers throughout the JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag are good - they are solid and well constructed like the rest of the bag, meaning we should get a good, long life out of it, whatever we throw at it. In fact, all the materials, construction, and design are outstanding. The outside of the bag is symmetrical, with matching slots/pockets on each side for your rackets and other items. Based on the depth and width, we’d carry balls in the main compartment, but the outside offers plenty of options. For the racket you’ll get sharped pockets with that kind of material you find inside a lot of cooler/cooler bags - the silver material that keeps it cool, allegedly for keeping your racket in a “temperate controlled” slot. Didn’t even think about having rackets stay ‘cool,’ but there you go. The JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag also offers a major, hard plastic hook in its own zippered pocket on the backside. You’ll be able to hang the bag, or set it, whatever you need, but do so with confidence of the quality of materials here. The bag also comes with not merely the handle on the top, but backpack straps to let you carry it with ease. Again, like the rest of the materials, the backpack straps are well made and should be comfortable for hauling around on your back.

In the end, this JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag is excellent and I’m thrilled to have it. We may be new to the sport of pickleball, but we’ve both spent our lives as athletes of various sports and had many bags over the years. I'm used to the ways of a good bag and thrilled with how well done this JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag is, how great it looks, and how it’ll make carrying my gear easy.

ALPS OutdoorZ Extreme Traverse X WOW! That's the first word that came to my mind when I opened the box this pack was delivered in. The last time I wore any backpack was when I was a Boy Scout--and that was about 55 years ago. I remember thinking what a great backpack that was. Its ability to swallow massive quantities of camping gear and personal items was impressive although there never seemed to be space for enough food to keep a growing 12 year old happy. The later addition of the first rudimentary frame was considered a luxury although comfort took a back seat to utility.

This ALPS OutdoorZ Extreme Traverse X Hunting Pack (whew) is the "Swiss Army Knife" of backpacks, providing enough features to be adaptable for several potential uses. It's a lot like one of those "pop out" RVs that provide additional space by expanding, but only when you need it. Otherwise it's a neat and efficient package. The frame is a molded of structural foam that fits the curve of your back, the wide straps are padded to ease the burden on your shoulders, and expanding the "wings" increases the comfort by keeping the pack stable around your middle. The construction is robust and uses high grade materials for the fabric, zippers, and buckles. A versatile design allows you to tailor its use to your particular needs. The camouflage pattern allows you to fade into the forest/wetlands should you need to make yourself unnoticeable.

Right now I am using this to carry guns, ammunition, water, insect repellent, sunscreen, targets, and various tools to the shooting range. Because I have a bad back, carrying a heavy duffle bag on one side of my body is a recipe for muscle spasms. Instead I can shoulder this pack, carry all of the stuff I need, and not risk hurting myself. Once I have really gotten comfortable with how to stuff as much as possible into this pack, I will start configuring it into my "bug out bag". If/when the SHTF you need to be able to shoulder a pack at a moment's notice with all the practical stuff you need to survive on your own until things cool off. Of course you also need to know that whatever you choose to take with you can be evenly distributed in your pack and that the weight doesn't become a limiting factor.

This pack is strong and versatile enough to be put to many different uses, and you can be comfortable knowing that it's built to last. This isn't just a hunting pack, it's an extremely versatile carry system.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS OutdoorZ Extreme Traverse X

text_fidelity_a: ALPS Mountaineering Zephyr 3-Person Tent Personally I love this tent. First, the price is great and you don't sacrifice quality. I started off with the two person version of this tent but then we got a dog... so three person tent it was! Second, it's a light tent for backpacking. I'm sure you could find something more expensive that packs slightly smaller but for the seasons we camp and hike, it's the perfect weight/size. third, without the rain fly you can just have 360 views of where ever you are camping or backpacking since the tent is mostly mesh. Lastly? It has the perfect rain fly. We accidentally tested it on one camping trip during a strong Colorado rain and hail storm. We had heavy rains almost all night and I kept waking myself with the fear that this little tent would shred or leak. We stayed perfectly dry and it even stood up to the pea hail we got. As long as the fly is tied down (wind can't blow it off the stakes) away from the tent, you and your items will stay dry.

text_fidelity_a:
Saver Pad Set I had an accident on my skateboard yesterday, hit my elbow pretty hard and quit for the day. I was going to wait for this protective gear before I started practicing Ollies or doing anything else risky, but my sore elbow was a good reminder to wait for the proper equipment to use before something like that (or worse) happened again.
This set of knee, elbow and wrist protectors is fairly well-made although light. The only thing I really don't like is the logo. After years in graphic-arts I have decided that I truly dislike high-visibility logos so I remove them by sanding or cutting them off. In the case of this "Triple-eight" with a horrible intersection of 3 eights the best method was flat black enamel paint that seems to have obliterated everything except the raised portions of the embroidery. Otherwise it's all black and low key. (This was my intent when I bought this kit and it worked well. Yay!)
The fit is fairly good for a mass-produced set of items, the big factor and the determination for S-M-L being the hand and wrist-guard, which I ordered Large. It's a little loose, but I have all sorts of foam sheets and leather pieces to custom-fit these important pieces, even to reinforcing the external portions as required. The knee and elbow pads are sort of a one-size-fits-all, but the same rules for modification apply.
Essentially, a very good buy for protection that is far better to have and not need than to really need and not have!
This is important stuff to wear, because a skateboard can become very dangerous suddenly without any warning. This kit, in conjunction with a decent helmet and good shoes (skate shoes) can make the difference in protecting those parts of your body that won't function very well unless they move freely without pain. Try being an artist or musician with a broken wrist. Try driving you car or riding your bike with a bad elbow or knee. It's in your best interest to protect yourself, because nobody else will, and if you still haven't figured it out getting hurt costs $$$!
text_fidelity_b: Saver Pad Set

text_fidelity_a:
JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control Speed
For aggressive players, this paddle comes up a little short. The weight of the paddle makes it seem like it's a heavy hitter, but the added rubber absorbs some of the energy so you lose power. Overall, you'll still get some great power shots but it won't improve your speed.

Spin
The spin on this paddle is very good and easy to produce. Right out of the package, you can tell the rubber is well made and has good traction. I was able to get good back/top/side spin without too much effort. In comparison to other Joola rackets I've owned, the spin is fairly good but it lacks some spin traction that I would expect. If you're coming from a basic racket (i.e. the cheap ones you see at discount stores) the spin on this paddle increase your spin game greatly.

Control
This is one area I felt this paddle excelled in. The grip, the 5-Ply real wood, the padding, everything about this paddle makes playing really easy. For someone who is getting more serious about their game, the added control to this racket is perfect. The control aspect of the racket is well balanced which can aid in improving your spin and attacks.

Overview
The Joola Infinity Balance Racket is well made recreational racket that is great for the enthusiast. The racket is decently padded for control and has decent spin capabilities. It's perfect for someone who isn't perfecting a particular playing style but just loves to play table tennis. It's very well balanced, feels great in the hand and had some decent power and spin.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control

Spree SmartCap with Integrated Heart Rate Monitor A cap that monitors your heart rate and temperature? What a great idea! Much better than the chest straps I've used in the past that always manage to tug on my chest hairs.

The Spree SmartCap works very well in my experience. While the monitor can be worn without the cap, it's easier to just have it installed in the cap that you can just put on and go. It paired effortlessly with my Nexus 4 phone using Bluetooth (despite the package says it only works with iPhones, they do provide an Android app now). The heart rate and temperature data seem to be fairly accurate.

With the GPS on, it is also compatible with some of the fitness apps I have for tracking my runs and bike rides. You'll get distance, speed, etc. that you can correlate to the heartrate and temperature. Unfortunately, the device is less suitable for the bike riding since the cap and even the band alone tends to get in the way of a helmet, though I did manage to get the band alone to sort of work with some tweaking.

I highly recommend The Spree for a very easy to use body monitor.
text_fidelity_b: Spree SmartCap with Integrated Heart Rate Monitor

CRKT Sting Fixed Blade Knife with Sheath: Everyday Carry Boot Knife, Double Edged Powder Coated Stainless Steel, Contoured Handle, Nylon Sheath with Strapping for Carry Options 2020 I was a little apprehensive about buying this knife in the first place. I didn't really NEED it, but it sure looked like a good idea and a good addition to my hiking/backpacking/fly fishing arsenal. First, let me say I was impressed with the quality. As a full piece of steel with a full tang, it is unlikely to separate at any time. While the handle is small owing to the size of the blade, it is still manageable. The handle has a nice big eyelet to which a safely line could be tied or, should one be in the mood, to use as a starter to tie to a branch to make a spear.

The sheath is also much better than I had expected. I had originally thought the sheath was just going to be straight nylon. This is not the case. There is a hard plastic liner within that secures the knife blade and keeps the blade from cutting up the sheath. Also, what looks like a thumb spot from the handle doubles as a non-mechanical locking mechanism within the sheath. It requires a decent tug to pull the knife out. This would certainly curtail accidental fallouts while walking or sprinting.

The nylon strap is both strong and adjustable. Overall, I'm quite impressed with this little gem.

text_fidelity_a:
Westt Mountain Bike Helmet - Bicycle Helmets for Adults with LED Rear Light - Scooter MTB Skateboard Baseball Cycling Helmet Between her roller blades and our eScooters, my wife and I needed two new bike helmets. This was the one we got her and so far, we really like it. I normally do not talk about price points, but in this case: for the price point it feels, looks, and acts like a solid choice. We hope to never have to find out about the "protective" elements, but hope it holds up to that standard as well.

1. The Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light is a good looking helmet, so if looks are important, this has a nice look to it. We like the blue we picked and the overall look is cool.

2. The fit is good. My wife has a smaller head than mine, so we got one that was very adjustable - not really by choice in that we would have order one "size specific" if needed, but again, for her needs. In this case, the Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light allows you to adjust the size in a "one size fits all" situation. The dial on the back adjusts for you and so far it works well. She likes the fit she gets and feels comfortable between that adjustment and the strap.

3. There is no way to "test" this helmet without falling - and we are not test dummies - so we must trust this will have the good if ever needed. She took a good spill once off a SEGWAY and had a helmet on - which truly saved her - and so we swear by wearing head gear. Here I jump to the idea of "You get what you pay for." The helmet we were able to get for me was a far higher price (here on Amazon, over $200), and you CAN tell a difference. BUT, that said, compared to our previous, similarly priced helmets, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light does seem to have what we need. Would we upgrade? Sure, who wouldn't? BUT, if price is a concern, and for most of us it is, would this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light do the trick? WE THINK SO. Again, there is NO way to know until you need it. text_fidelity_a:
Spec-Ops Brand Better BDU Belt 1.5-Inch I needed a BDU belt that would effectively fit my cargo shorts and hold up my IWB holster while carrying a Springfield .45 Mod 2. After researching various belts it became obvious that I needed a 1.5" wide belt to fit my belt loops, it had to be flexible enough to be comfortable around my surgically repaired abdomen, and it had to be strong enough to hold my Mod 2 in the right position for an effective draw. Since Florida is a concealed carry state, although they are currently considering open carry, my rig has to avoid printing so that it doesn't point out that I have a CCW in my possession. No sense in attracting unwanted attention from the public and law enforcement.

Over the years I have slowly moved up from carrying a NAA .22 magnum to a Kahr 9mm. The NAA .22 magnum is easily carried in any pocket with no printing issues. Stepping up to the Kahr 9mm was as easy as using a Sticky Holster inside my right front pocket. But carrying a far heavier and bulkier .45 took a little planning and trial and error. The clothing and belt have to be right, the carry position simple to access, and the weapon has to be concealed from public view.

I have the correct combination now thanks to this Spec-Ops BDU belt. It fits my regular belt loops, fastens securely around my waist, holds the weapon and holster in the proper position, is very comfortable, and instills the confidence needed when carrying a heavier weapon. I highly recommend this belt as a cost effective solution to carrying bulkier weapons.

As another interesting observation, each belt comes with a one page instruction sheet with illustrations. text_fidelity_a:
MSC® Boat Center Console Cover, Color Gray,Pacific Blue Available It seems OK ...

I'm giving it five stars to start with because it is what it said it would be and it fits my center console very well. It looks a lot nicer than the green plastic tarp I was using to keep my console dry. I ordered and received the gray color option.

It's fairly lightweight and folds/rolls up into a nice small package when it's stored in the bag that came with the cover. Most boaters will appreciate that as stowage on a boat is always at a premium. Putting it in its little bag keeps it from catching the wind and blowing away when towing the boat or on the water.

I've only had it for a couple of weeks so time will tell regarding longevity. The problem with most of these things is that they either last or they don't. If it falls apart in an unreasonable amount of time I'll be back to add to this review. I consider 5 years on a fabric cover of any type to be a "reasonable amount of time" for them to remain serviceable. Properly treated exterior grade fabrics should last quite a while. I have a Bimini top that has been on my boat for 15 years and it's still in serviceable condition. The top is deployed from April to October and I tow the boat with it up (it's only 3 miles to the ramp and it's 45 MPH or less speed limit all the way) so that's a good example of good service from an exterior grade fabric.

For some reason unknown to me the drawstring is NOT as shown in the item description. It's not on the aft side of the console where the drawstring and the cutout are located in the picture. It's on the starboard side of the console. Which is a little irritating because that's the side I usually store tackle boxes, coolers etc. to keep them handy to the helm and the fore deck both. So I have to move stuff around to use this console cover, which is not a big deal or a deal killer but I do wish these sellers would get their act together and provide ACCURATE pictures of what they're selling and we're buying.

Because while I like online shopping for the huge array of choices and the availability of things I may or may not find locally, or may have to drive miles to find and still might not be successful -- online shopping is always a crapshoot. You can't pick up and look at what you're buying, you can't walk in a store and see it set up on display so that you can examine its construction and quality. All you have to go by are pictures, item description and subjective reviews of others who have purchased the item. So it would seem to me that if sellers don't want to get returns and charge-backs they ought to pay very close attention to their pictures and item descriptions.
text_fidelity_b: MSC® Boat Center Console Cover, Color Gray,Pacific Blue Available

The LCD display is easy to read and understand. The security strap with a little clip helps keep it from getting lost. I love it and highly recommend it.

The first couple of weeks my wife and I just enjoyed talking about how many steps we had done that day. Then about a week ago I found the "aerobic STEP" display. If you walk 60 steps or more per minute for 10 minutes or more the pedometer displays this as "aerobic" steps. Walking articles suggest 30 minutes a day of "aerobic" walking. With the pedometer you can record an easy pace of 60-80 steps per minute for 30 minutes during a lunch break. Or split it into two sessions of 15 minutes and let the pedometer add them together. The picture I uploaded shows 3396 aerobic steps I did 5 days ago. It took me 34 minutes so that's about 100 steps a minute. For me 100 is a very easy pace to maintain (on level ground, good shoes, etc.) but even a slower 60 a minute is perfectly OK.

So thanks OMRON for adding this much needed activity to my life and helping me measure it. Gadgets are great and this one is highly recommended. $[...] is a real bargain for such proven health benefits.

That being said, I certainly don't have any complaints.

I really like the grind. I was able to play with some knock downs from tight lies, hit full shots from the back and front of my stance, even hit a few wide open flops (yeah I know a 52 really isn't the club). In all cases I was able to make clean contact.

The feel isn't what I would call "pure", but it was fine. A bit clicky to me, but as far as my game goes I am not going to consider that a negative. Some more accomplished players may see that as a bad thing.

The lie isn't right for me, I seemed to pull most shots with a slight draw. The opposite of my current clubs as I normally fade them. We will see how that plays on the course, but that's on me, not the club.

Bottom line: Let's face it, a functional club for an extremely affordable price is something we all can use. This club fits the situation perfectly.

Skiboards Ski boards 99cm with Tyrolia releasable Bindings New set and they were awesome. This was my first experience with snow blades and I bought them on a whim. I am an experienced skier and usually opt for longer skis (180ish). The skis came pre-sharpened and waxed from the factory.

I took them out to Whiteface Mtn in New York. Took me about 2 hours to get used them and transition from normal skies. By the end of the day I was able to hit the double black diamonds and technical trails without any trouble. Snow blades are a bit different as they excel on packed powder, ice, and machine groomed snow (which, sadly, is what you usually get at most mountains on the east coast!). In light powder, the blades tend to sink due to the low amount of surface area, which slows you down. Additionally, I found that the blades were not as stable if you try to rocket straight down a hill- carving your way down is the best technique for snow blades.

Lastly, I found that the blades made it a bit harder to land jumps well. Since they aren't as long as normal skis, you don't have the same amount of forgiveness with your landings and need to make sure that you come down straight & balanced.

Overall, the skis are totally worth the price considering a regular pair of skis is easily 4x the cost.
text_fidelity_b: Skiboards Ski boards 99cm with Tyrolia releasable Bindings New set

text_fidelity_a:
Aquasana Premium Borosilicate Glass Bottle with Designer Silicone Sleeve and BPA Free Lid with Stainless Steel Cover, 550ml, Blue I've wanted a glass bottle for some time, so I was excited to get this. It's 9" tall, a 2.75" diameter at the bottom, and holds about 18 fluid ounces. The bottle is made from borosilicate glass, so it's strong (for glass) and more resistant to heat or cold shock than soda-lime glass. The outer, threaded part on the lid contains plastic, but the parts that contact the liquid are a metal inner "plug" and an O-ring. The lid is easy to screw on (and I have weak hands). I've not had any leaks when the bottle tips over with the lid on.

The mouth of the bottle is 1 1/8" across on the inside. If you're getting water from the faucet, it's easy enough to fill the bottle. I've ended up using a funnel when filling the bottle with my hot tea, though, as I apparently don't have a consistently steady hand. I can get a bottle brush into the bottle's mouth, though you can also put the bottle through the dish washer.

I've got size "medium womens" hands, and I've never felt like I might drop the bottle as the cross-hatch silicone sleeve design provides a good grip. The bottom of the sleeve covers the entire bottom of the bottle, which provides some padding and non-slip effect. The cross-hatch design allows my fingers to contact the hot (from my tea) side, though. I just wait for the tea to cool, but that might not be convenient for some people. Obviously, this bottle isn't insulated, so the liquid will cold or warm up to room temperature fairly quickly. It's a nice bottle.
text_fidelity_b: Aquasana Premium Borosilicate Glass Bottle with Designer Silicone Sleeve and BPA Free Lid with Stainless Steel Cover, 550ml, Blue

Benchmade - Nimravus 141SBK Knife, Tanto Blade, Serrated Edge, Coated Finish, Black Handle, Made in the USA I collect knives and hatchets--but I think that my wife considers it hoarding. Probably a fine line there. I had previously looked at a Benchmade Infidel, an OTF automatic, but found it to be of lesser quality than my Microtechs. It also had a lot of blade play (slop) which always makes me doubt the construction quality. I finally got seduced by a picture of a Benchmade Bedlam. It just plain looked wicked and I had to have it. Unfortunately it also lacked in quality.

Benchmade's fixed blade knives have always had a great reputation. I saw the Nimravus at a gun and knife show and was impressed by the weight and balance. It was solidly built in the mode of my Busse fixed blades. It is sinister looking, built like a tank with a very sharp tanto blade, and has the look of a weapon that would get my attention immediately if it were pulled on me. The overall size is almost perfect, it fits my hands well, the construction is robust, and it is extremely well-balanced.

Always remember to use extreme caution when handling knives. An old-timer once told me that they are just as dangerous as guns because they are always loaded. One slip can have disastrous results. So until you can go to Walmart and buy a new finger, or can print one with a 3D printer, be careful out there.
text_fidelity_b: Benchmade - Nimravus 141SBK Knife, Tanto Blade, Serrated Edge, Coated Finish, Black Handle, Made in the USA

Morpilot 20PSI Paddle Board Pump - Dual Stage Inflation with Powerful SUP Pump Inflator & Deflator, Auto-Off, AC & DC, Intelligent Preset - Perfect for Inflatable Stand-Up Paddle Boards I ordered this item to have a handy way to inflate a slam ball after they lose air over time. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. However, this little unit worked incredibly well.

It charges quickly via USB Micro (120 minutes to full charge / with 30 inflates per charge), has all of the accessories needed to get going (USB cable, air needles, attachment hose, etc..), has pre-set modes for a football, a soccer ball, a basketball, etc.. And is super compact & lightweight (6.29" x 1.4" & weighing only 6.5oz).

I haven't tried, but don't see why you couldn't even inflate a bicycle tire with this unit as well. However, I probably wouldn't try with anything larger like a car or truck tire out of concern of damaging the pump.

There is an auto-shut off option (IE: when you use a ball preset the pump will turn off when it dispenses the appropriate amount of air for the selected ball), however, there is no pressure gauge. So, if you don't use the preset, then you have to go by feel (or have an air gauge on hand).

As far as my experiment, I didn't even use the presets. Just popped in the needle into my slam ball & turned on the pump. It inflated (my very deflated) slam ball in a matter of seconds. A success!

If you're constantly using a foot pump or bike pump to inflate your sports equipment, bike tires, etc.., then seriously consider this portable pump instead. Makes this process super easy. There's even an attachment that looks like it's to be used for blowing up balloons! Very cool!
text_fidelity_b: Morpilot 20PSI Paddle Board Pump - Dual Stage Inflation with Powerful SUP Pump Inflator & Deflator, Auto-Off, AC & DC, Intelligent Preset - Perfect for Inflatable Stand-Up Paddle Boards

text_fidelity_a:
JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes The UPS deliveryman carried this box to the front door with ease, but I quickly learned that a 108 lb., smooth, cardboard box is NOT that easy to maneuver. So just be aware this is a heavy shipment!

I was worried this was going to be a cheap and flimsy bike, but that's not the case in any way! This thing is welded, heavy gauge steel with a thick paint job (probably not powder coated). The handles are equally solid with a thick rubber grip, probably hot dipped. Basically, no amount of sweaty hands are going to cause the grip to deteriorate. The mechanics are practically silent.

Assembly is a cinch. There are 4 bolts used to attach the feet, three adjustable handles to attach the seat and handle, and two pedals to screw on. All of the required tools are in the box.

I've only ridden on it once, but the seat is soft (not that it matters if you're standing). The electronic display is of utmost cheapness, though. I was afraid that I was going to break it when installing the (included) AA batteries. It provides very basic information such as time, distance, "speed", and "calories" but there is no input for height and weight.

I'm waiting on a cadence sensor that will attach to one of the crank arms, and plan to use that with an app to get better feedback on pace. I also downloaded the Peloton app (30 day free trial) and was able to follow along just fine with the beginners ride. The resistance knob doesn't have a numeric scale (just +/-) so you'll have to judge for yourself based on how it feels.

Final thought is regarding the maneuverability. The front wheels are a bit small and made of a hard plastic so it will be hard to roll across carpet. You can tell from the photo we have a hard floor, and if it gets caught on debris, it may easily get stuck or scratch the floor.

Overall, I'm impressed with the build quality, assembly and performance. Only negatives are the ultra cheap display, lack of any integrated wireless technology (BYO), and the small wheels to move it around.
text_fidelity_b: JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes

text_fidelity_a:
Yes4All Versatile Wooden Wobble Balance Trainer Board with 360 Degree Rotation I love this amazing balance board. I've tried out quite a few balance boards, and this one is the absolute best of this style. The thing that I like most about it is that it's very comfortable to use when I just have my bare feet. I mostly use it with shoes, but I really like that I have the option of using it with just bare feet.

The whole surface has a grip coating. It's kind of like what they have on skateboards, but like I said, this is much more comfortable to stand on with your bare feet. If you're super uncoordinated like me, then you might be wondering if you should wait until you're stronger to start working on your balance. But, I totally recommend this to be one the first pieces of fitness equipment that you get. The biggest reason is that it's pretty easy to balance on, and when you're balancing then you generally aren't locking your knees, which is the biggest reason why beginners get injured.

The other thing that I really like about this is that the bottom is smooth. This might not seem like a very important feature, but with this style of balance board, it actually is, because all of your weight gets concentrated into a very tiny area on the floor. If the bottoms of these aren't smooth, they will indent even the hardest of floors. So, because it has a smooth bottom, then it makes it perfect to use on almost any surface. True, it does slip just a tiny bit, over a grip surface, but I don't mind a little slipping because it's supposed to be teaching me balance.

The construction of this is great. It's about seven layers of board, stuck together. The bottom is an extremely firmly secured piece of very sturdy plastic. Overall, this is an awesome balance board. It's awesome for beginners like me, but if you're already a fitness expert and in awesome shape, then I really think you'll like it too.

*Yes4All gave me this board to review*
text_fidelity_b: Yes4All Versatile Wooden Wobble Balance Trainer Board with 360 Degree Rotation

SANSBUG 1-Person Popup Screen Tent (Tarp Floor) This net is great and can even be used as a one person tent in clear weather. This seals completely, unlike the big hanging nets that hang down around you but leave the floor or ground exposed.

Setup takes all of 10 seconds, including taking the tent out of the bag and throwing the tent in the air to let it pop up on its own. You don't have to worry about tying anything off, but it does come with stakes if you want to use it outdoors as tent. Storage is easy and it folds float in about a 30" ring.

I'm 5'9" tall and overweight, and I had plenty of leg room and room on either side and could sit up and move around inside the tent. I also have room for a few vital pieces of gear that I wanted to keep with me. If your over 6' tall your mileage may vary.

I set my tent up on a cot at our local Boy Scout summer camp inside a permanent canvass tent that didn't completely seal. It fit pretty well on the cot, with just a little overhang on either side of the cot.

My son and his tent mate each had one of these, and they had to reposition their cots so they ran from side to side instead of front to back to avoid downward pressure from the sloping tent roof. The sloping ends of this cot then fit the roofline of the tent very well.

I have slept in this for 3 nights so far and my son has slept in his 6 nights. It seems well made and like it will hold up well.
text_fidelity_b: SANSBUG 1-Person Popup Screen Tent (Tarp Floor)

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish I purchased this knife as a semi-impulse buy. I had been looking for a new edc for a couple months, however I was skeptic to stray away from my kershaw of 5 years.

After my initial purchase I read many mixed reviews, and after a month of carrying here are my thoughts.

PROS:
1) The low profile pocket clip doesn't scratch the crap out of my car paint as my kershaw did.
2) The metal is not as good as my kershaw, but it is VERY VERY close.
3) A ceramic hone works best after sharpening.
4) You can get this thing RAZOR sharp, but it dulls after a moderate amount of use.
5) It is SUPER light, and very fast.
6) Initially the opening mechanism is weird getting used to. However once you do, it is actually very easy to use.
7) The short blade does NOT impede its performance as I originally thought. You can think the belly of the knife for this, it adds a nice additional cutting surface.
8) The anodized aluminum is fairly slip resistant.
9) The thumb studs protrude enough for you to get a good open on it.
10) It is very sleek looking and the POP is an attention getter.
11) It is pretty ergonomic and it fits in the hand pretty well.

CONS:
1) It is difficult getting adjusted to the opening mechanism.
2) The "safety" makes me feel like this thing will jump open in my pocket if I don't have it turned on.... even though it probably wont.
3) I don't care for lock back knives as it impedes one handed use. I now can use it one handed though which took some practice.
4) The metal is odd, things you think would dull it won't.... but the things you don't think would will.. I.E. it cuts through weed eater string like a beast but a couple pieces of thin cardboard has this blade spent.
5) Tape and other adhesives stick to this blade BAD... My kershaw had a Teflon coating. Something I wished this one had.
6) the top of the pocket clip sticks up about 3/16 of an inch from the knife.... it is just odd to me. It doesn't really affect the functionality however.

Even though I questioned my purchase at first, I am very happy with my purchase. For this price you get a PERFECT edc knife. Just make sure that you have at least an 800-1200 grit diamond stone and a ceramic hone for quick sharpening.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer This is a simple and easy to assembly bike rack. It works perfect for us.

it took me all of 15 minutes to put together for 3 bikes. I love that you have the option to expand it to 5 bikes if needed. (more on that later). The instructions were easy to follow (I've included a pic).

What's in the box: This comes with everything you need to assemble your frame, even a little hex wrench which is the only tool you need other than your two hands. All the pieces are nicely packed in the box and have plastic over them to protect them from getting scuffed up in the box. Your box should have 2 frame tube ends, 10 frame tubes, 10 wheel arms, 5 wheel arm binders, 20 hex-head screws, and one hex wrench.

Assembly: The bottom bars for the frame pretty much snap together with little push in metal buttons to hold them in place (see pic). The holes for the buttons are nice and oblong so you have room to twist/maneuver them when attaching the wheel arms to get the holes aligned when screwing them in. The only slight issue I had is the hex screw heads. A few of them seemed to easily strip when I was doing the last few turns with the provided hex wrench. I was not even tightening them very tight so there was not a lot of torque. I figured they were probably just cheap screws, but they still did the job fine. The screws you can twist by hand easily once you get the holes aligned correctly then just use the hex wrench to finish up. Once you have the wheel arms attached the wheel arm binders easily attach at the top of the wheel arms but squeezing them together slightly then just slide the binder down next to the frame once it is on. And that's all there is to it!

using the stand: we have 3 bikes - 2 mountain bikes and 1 road bike. I thought I may have to add a spacer to the frame since the mountain bike handle bars will not fit if the two of them are right next to each other in this stand. I did try putting one in backward, with the rear wheel in the stand, but the bike stand arms were too narrow for wheel and derailer to completely fit into the stand. however, my road bike is small enough that it fits just under the mountain bike handle bars. putting that in the middle solved the issue! Now we have all three bikes neatly parked in a corner of the garage rather than leaning against the wall and boxes. yay! And if we happen to acquire more bikes, we can always expand it.

Overall this is a decent, simple bike stand that does what we need.
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer
